2609.03915.title: RuleMem: Active Rule Memory for Long-Term Conversational Agents
2609.03915.paper_summary: Question answering agents in long-term conversations must reason over massive, temporally dispersed dialogue histories. However, existing memory mechanisms primarily treat past information as \textit{passively} stored facts, leading to semantic gaps and unreliable reasoning. To address this limitation, we propose RuleMem, a rule-based memory framework that induces reusable logical rules from historical interactions to \textit{actively} guide both evidence retrieval and reasoning. Specifically, RuleMem constructs natural-language Horn clauses from conversations and validates them via a Rule Perplexity Consistency (RPC) mechanism. These induced rules enable the retrieval of semantically distant evidence while providing an explicit logical structure for answer generation. We conducted a comprehensive evaluation of RuleMem on two long-term conversational benchmarks, LoCoMo and LongMemEval_s*. In a rigorous comparison against 14 baselines on LoCoMo, RuleMem achieved the highest accuracy, exceeding the baseline average by 27.47 points (a 54.3% relative improvement).
2609.03915.paper_summary_zh: 長期對話中的問答代理必須對大量時間上分散的對話歷史進行推理。然而，現有的記憶機制主要將過去的信息視為\textit{被動}存儲的事實，這導致了語義上的差距和不可靠的推理。為了解決這一限制，我們提出了RuleMem，一種基於規則的記憶框架，從歷史互動中誘導可重用的邏輯規則，以\textit{主動}指導證據檢索和推理。具體而言，RuleMem從對話中構建自然語言的霍恩子句，並通過規則困惑度一致性（RPC）機制進行驗證。這些誘導的規則使得檢索語義上遙遠的證據成為可能，同時為答案生成提供了明確的邏輯結構。我們對RuleMem在兩個長期對話基準LoCoMo和LongMemEval_s*上進行了全面評估。在對LoCoMo的14個基準進行嚴格比較中，RuleMem達到了最高的準確率，超過基準平均值27.47分（相對提高54.3%）。
